item.title: agent-pawl
item.description:
pawl ensures your AI coding agents follow the steps you want, in the order you want.

You write a workflow as a YAML state machine, and pawl drives the agent through it, not moving on until a step’s check passes. Deterministic steps run as scripts, agentic steps are handed to subagents, and postconditions are checked by pawl itself, so the agent can’t simply declare the job done.

It ships as a Claude Code plugin with a bundled Go binary, a skill and enforcement hooks. Check it out on GitHub.

item.title: Budgebell
item.description:
An agent-first desktop app that nudges you through habits (movement drills first, general habits too), shows you what to do, and logs what you actually did.

It’s designed to be driven by an AI agent rather than by hand: a bundled local MCP server lets your agent add, update and disable habits, decide what you get nudged about, and read back the log of what you did or skipped.

Everything stays on your machine: habit definitions, media and logs, with no network calls, no telemetry and no cloud (the MCP server is local too). Built with Tauri and Svelte, with releases for macOS, Linux and Windows.

item.title: pylemmy
item.description:
pylemmy enables simple access to the API of Lemmy, the federated link aggregator, from Python.

On top of it I built lemmy-summarizer, a Lemmy bot that summarizes the news articles linked in posts, using trafilatura to extract the article text and a Hugging Face transformers model to summarize it.

item.title: Toxic News
item.description:
A website enabling automatic ranking of online media outlets using machine learning models (for now, only using Unitary.ai’s detoxify model).

Once per day, the headlines from the frontpage of multiple online media outlets are scraped, and sent to machine learning models. The results are displayed in the website.

It runs entirely as a scheduled GitHub Actions job, with git as the only store: no database and no server.

Check out the website at https://toxicnews.dcferreira.com, and have a look at the About page for more details

item.title: Tweet Fake
item.description:
This was a short project I did with a pick-up team for a weekend-long Hackathon. The idea was to take the most liked tweets for a specific user, and use a Large Language Model to generate new tweets in this user’s style.

The demo is no longer online, but there is a short video in the devpost project page.

item.title: Infinity for Youtube
item.description:
A simple browser extension that hides YouTube video length for user-selected channels. Unlike other similar browser extensions, this one also hides the video length in video thumbnails.

You can easily install it from the Chrome Web Store.

item.title: City-GAN
item.description: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are a well-known technique that is trained on samples (e.g. pictures of fruits) and which after training is able to generate realistic new samples. Conditional GANs (CGANs) additionally provide label information for subclasses (e.g. apple, orange, pear) which enables the GAN to learn more easily and increase the quality of its output samples. We use GANs to learn architectural features of major cities and to generate images of buildings which do not exist. We show that currently available GAN and CGAN architectures are unsuited for this task and propose a custom architecture and demonstrate that our architecture has superior performance for this task and verify its capabilities with extensive experiments.
